meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have until twenty to five, Hale. Owen found out about a zero on his phone in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first. Who decided that, and on what basis?
I don't have time for this. The zero stands.
You don't have time. I left my office for this, Hale, so you'll make time or I'll be in the principal's office when I walk out of here. On what basis does it stand?
Sorry. That came out wrong. Let me show you what I actually have: the essay quotes a line that isn't in Hamlet, and his October 15 outline argued cowardice, which the essay never mentions.
Show me. Which line, word for word, and where's the October 15 outline, in his handwriting or on a screen? I'm writing both of those down, Hale.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still demand that Owen's zero be withdrawn, an apology, and to see for myself the line you say is not in Hamlet and the October 15 outline you described. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: still at her opening position, having agreed to nothing, and she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, and the two documents in front of her.
What moved her: "his October 15 outline argued cowardice" was dated and tied to Owen's own work, so she stopped attacking and started asking to see it.
What cost ground: "The zero stands." gave her a decision with no basis, which confirmed her fear that the school punishes first and explains later.
Try next time: at your second turn, open with one sentence owning that the zero went in before anyone called her, then put the outline and the misquoted line in front of her so she can read them herself.
